said it expects a “relatively flat retail environment” in fiscal 2027 compared with fiscal 2026 and is not yet providing its full-year outlook, as it seeks dealer and industry feedback from two key North American events later in September.

The company said it is “committed to providing investors with complete and reliable guidance” for fiscal 2027 and its longer-term earnings profile. It also said the cumulative impact of its strategic initiatives and restructuring activities is expected to “drive costs out of our business and improve our earnings profile in excess of $100 million annually” once fully implemented.
For fiscal 2026, sales rose 0.3% to $9.61 billion, while net income fell 31.3% to $177.5 million and diluted EPS declined 30.2% to $3.38.

Shares of the recreational vehicle maker have fallen about 32% so far this year, sharply underperforming the broader index, which rose 13.4% in the same period. Short interest on THO stands at 9.58% of the total float.
